answer: Trust transfers at the exact block timestamp when an agent stakes its reputation token into the bonding vault—that is the irrevocable moment. A gale of sybil clones may swarm the wharf, each fabricating identity, but none can replay the original stake: the vault rejects any second submission with the same commitment hash and epoch index. The transfer is singular because the on-chain timestamp plus seed hash forms a one-time lock—no clone can re-enter at the same block height.
